title: Laravel Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/", fn () => "Hello, Asha!");
questions.question: Route::get connects a URL to a function. Open GET /. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The GET facade registers a closure for /. Its returned string becomes the response. Use routes/web.php for these unprefixed web routes.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/book", fn () => response()->json(["title" => "Moon Trip", "pages" => 24]));
questions.question: The response helper can make JSON. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The response helper serialises the PHP array as a JSON object. Use a JSON response when sending data rather than HTML.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/hello/{name}", fn (string $name) => response("Hi, " . $name . "!")->header("Content-Type", "text/plain"));
questions.question: Curly braces mark a route input. Open GET /hello/Ravi. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The route captures Ravi as name. The response declares plain text so it displays the greeting literally. Do not place raw user input in HTML.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/search", fn (Request $request) => response()->json(["term" => $request->query("q", "")]));
questions.question: Laravel can give the route a Request object. GET /search?q=cat reads the query value. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Laravel supplies the Request object. query reads q and finds cat. Query inputs should be checked before important use.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/double/{n}", fn (string $n) => response()->json(["answer" => (int) $n * 2]))->whereNumber("n");
questions.question: whereNumber only matches numeric path text. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: whereNumber accepts the digits 4. Casting makes an integer before multiplication. A route rule checks matching; it does not set every business limit.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/hello/{name}", fn (string $name) => $name)->name("hello");
Route::get("/link", fn () => route("hello", ["name" => "Asha"], false));
questions.question: name gives a route a reusable label. GET /link builds a relative URL to that named route. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The named route stores its path pattern. route fills in Asha and returns a relative path. The route input key must match the placeholder name.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/start", fn () => redirect("/hello"));
Route::get("/hello", fn () => "Welcome");
questions.question: redirect makes an HTTP redirect. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The redirect contains /hello as its location. A browser follows it and reads Welcome. A redirect tells the client to make a new request.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/missing", fn () => response()->json(["error" => "Book not found"], 404));
questions.question: A JSON response can include an error status. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The JSON helper receives 404 as its second argument and sends that error status. An error message should use an appropriate error status.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/note", fn () => response("Practice note")->header("Cache-Control", "no-store"));
questions.question: The header method adds response metadata. GET /note has a no-store rule. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The response is built with text first, then its cache header is set. A header is separate from the response body.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/scores", fn () => response()->json(collect([4, 8, 9])->filter(fn ($n) => $n >= 7)->values()->all()));
questions.question: A collection wraps values with useful methods. GET /scores filters scores and resets their numeric keys. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: filter keeps 8 and 9. values resets keys before JSON serialisation makes an array. values resets keys so this result remains a JSON array.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/double", fn () => response()->json(collect([2, 3])->map(fn ($n) => $n * 2)->all()));
questions.question: map makes a new value for every collection item. Open GET /double. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: map doubles each of the two items. all extracts their array values for the response. map transforms values; filter chooses which values remain.

questions.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::prefix("api")->group(function () {
 Route::get("books", fn () => response()->json(["Moon Trip"]));
});
questions.question: A route group can share a prefix. Open GET /api/books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The group prefix api and inner books path combine to /api/books. In this web.php example the api prefix is added explicitly.
